title: Build Your First Web Page: Gritt-ify
summary: Make a small fan page for Gritty from scratch. You will set up project folders, write the page's content, connect a style file, and add colors, sizes and spacing.
outcome: A two-part web page with a purple banner, a small Gritty picture, a big Gritter title, a message form and a list of funny posts.
learns: The basic shape of a web page

files.content:
Gritty's landing banner

Cause everything's better with Gritty's face on it.

Gritter

Social media dedicated to Gritty... and only Gritty... cause he's a psycho.

  • Hey there, it's Gritty again.
  • I haven't eaten any other mascots since yesterday.
  • Burp.

steps.title: What we're building
steps.instruction: Watch the introduction to see the Gritty fan page you will build and what you will learn.
steps.why: Knowing the goal makes each step make sense.
hints: Just watch this part.
Notice the two parts of the page: a banner and a social feed.
Nothing to type yet.

steps.title: Make the project folders
steps.instruction: Watch how the project folder is made. Inside it there is a file called index.html and a folder called resources, which holds a css folder (with an empty index.css file) and an images folder.
steps.why: A tidy folder layout makes it easy to point files at each other.
hints: Just watch and copy the folder layout on your computer.
You need index.html, resources/css/index.css and resources/images.
Nothing to type in the code yet.

concept.title: Project folders
concept.explain: A website is just files in folders, and keeping pictures and styles in their own folders keeps things tidy.

steps.title: Add the Gritty picture
steps.instruction: Watch the picture file better_than_drake.png get copied into the resources/images folder. Put any picture with that name there yourself.
steps.why: The page will show this picture, so it has to live inside the project.
hints: Just watch this part.
The picture goes in resources/images.
Name it better_than_drake.png.

steps.title: The page skeleton
steps.instruction: In index.html, type the basic shape of a web page: the first line saying it's HTML, an html wrapper, a head with the page title Gritt-ify and a link to your style file, and an empty body.
steps.why: Every web page needs this frame before any content goes in.

checks.say: I can't see the page title Gritt-ify yet.
Your page isn't connected to the style file yet.
checks.name: href

checks.say: I can't find the body part of your page.

hints: Start with the line that tells the browser this is an HTML page, then build a head and a body inside an html wrapper.
The title tag goes inside head, and so does a link tag pointing to ./resources/css/index.css.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <title>…</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="…">
</head>
…

concept.title: Head and body
concept.explain: The head holds information about the page, like its title, while the body holds everything people actually see.
concept.imageQuery: html page structure head body diagram

steps.title: Page settings
steps.instruction: Right after the opening head line, add three meta lines: one for the text format, one so the page fits phones, and one for older browsers.
steps.why: These settings make text show correctly and the page fit any screen.
steps.expected:
<meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <meta http-equiv="X-UA-Compatible" content="ie=edge">

checks.say: I can't see the text format setting yet.
The setting that makes the page fit phones is missing.
checks.name: content

hints: Add three small setting lines at the top of the head.
Each is a meta tag; the first sets charset to UTF-8.

<meta charset="UTF-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="…">
<meta http-equiv="…" content="ie=edge">

concept.title: Meta tags
concept.explain: Meta tags are hidden settings that tell the browser how to read and size your page.

steps.title: The banner section
steps.instruction: Inside the body, add a note saying Banner section, then a box (div) labelled with the class banner. Inside it put a big heading, the Gritty picture with the id small-gritty, a short sentence, and a button.
steps.why: This is the first thing visitors see at the top of the page.
steps.expected:
Gritty's landing banner

Cause everything's better with Gritty's face on it.

checks.say: I can't see the banner box with its big heading yet.
The Gritty picture isn't pointing at the picture file yet.
checks.name: src

checks.say: The button is missing from the banner.

hints: Make one box that holds a heading, a picture, a sentence and a button.
Use a div with class="banner", then h1, img, p and button inside it.

concept.title: Classes and ids
concept.explain: A class or id is a name tag on part of your page, so you can style it later.

steps.title: The Gritter section
steps.instruction: Below the banner, add a note saying Gritter section, then a new box. Inside it put the word Gritter with the id gritter, a sentence with the class bold, and a form with a text box and a Submit button.
steps.why: This section is a pretend social feed just for Gritty.
steps.expected:
Gritter

Social media dedicated to Gritty... and only Gritty... cause he's a psycho.

checks.say: I can't see the Gritter title yet.
The form with a Submit button is missing.
The sentence with the bold label isn't there yet.

hints: Make a second box under the banner with a title, a sentence and a little form.
Use span id="gritter", p class="bold", and a form with two input tags.

concept.title: Forms
concept.explain: A form lets visitors type something and press a button to send it.

steps.title: The first post
steps.instruction: Right after the form ends, add a bulleted list with one item holding Gritty's first post: Hey there, it's Gritty again.
steps.why: A list is a natural way to show a feed of posts.

checks.say: I can't see the list of posts yet.
Gritty's first post isn't showing yet.

hints: Add a list under the form with one post in it.
Use ul for the list and li for each item; the post text goes in a span.

• …
    • …

concept.title: Lists
concept.explain: A ul makes a bulleted list, and each li inside it is one bullet point.

steps.title: Relative paths
steps.instruction: Watch how the picture's address ./resources/images/better_than_drake.png works: it starts from where index.html is and walks into the folders.
steps.why: Paths are how one file finds another in your project.
hints: Just watch this part.
The dot means start from this folder.
Each slash steps into the next folder.

concept.title: Relative paths
concept.explain: A relative path is directions to a file, starting from the file you're writing in.

steps.title: Open it in the browser
steps.instruction: Watch the page get opened in Chrome. Open your index.html in your browser too and look at the plain, unstyled page.
steps.why: Checking in the browser shows what you've built so far.
hints: Just watch, then try it yourself.
Double-click index.html or drag it into a browser.
It looks plain because there are no styles yet.

steps.title: More posts
steps.instruction: After the first post's list item, add two more list items: one saying I haven't eaten any other mascots since yesterday. and one saying Burp.
steps.why: A feed with a few posts looks more real.
steps.expected:
• I haven't eaten any other mascots since yesterday.
  • Burp.

checks.say: Your list should have three posts in it.
I can't see the Burp post yet.

hints: Copy the shape of the first post twice, with new words.
Add two more li items inside the ul, right after the first one.

• I haven't eaten …
    • …

steps.title: Style the banner
steps.instruction: Open resources/css/index.css. Write a rule for the banner class that makes the background purple (#4D00FF), the text white, adds 75px of space above, and centers the text. Refresh the browser to see it.
steps.why: This is your first style rule, and it changes how the banner looks.

checks.say: The banner isn't purple yet.
The banner text isn't centered yet.

hints: Start with the banner's name, then list the looks you want between curly brackets.
A class rule starts with a dot: .banner, then background-color, color, margin-top and text-align.

concept.title: A style rule
concept.explain: A style rule names what to change, then lists looks like color and size inside curly brackets.

steps.title: How the style file connects
steps.instruction: Watch how the link line in the head connects index.css to the page, using a path just like the picture did.
steps.why: Without that link, the page never sees your styles.
hints: Just watch this part.
Look at the link line you typed in the head.
Its address points to ./resources/css/index.css.

concept.title: Linking a style file
concept.explain: The link tag in the head tells the page which style file to use.

steps.title: Shrink Gritty and add space
steps.instruction: Inside the banner rule, add 100px of padding on the top and bottom. Then below the banner rule, write a rule for the id small-gritty that makes the picture 100px tall and 100px wide.
steps.why: A smaller picture and some breathing room make the banner look neat.

checks.say: The Gritty picture isn't small yet.
The banner needs more space at the top and bottom.

hints: Give the banner padding, then make a new rule for the picture's id.
An id rule starts with #: #small-gritty with height and width. Padding goes inside .banner.

concept.title: Ids and padding
concept.explain: A # picks one named part of the page, and padding adds space inside its edges.

steps.title: Big Gritter title
steps.instruction: Below the small-gritty rule, write a rule for the id gritter that makes the text purple (#4D00FF) and 100px big.
steps.why: A huge colorful title makes the Gritter section stand out.

checks.say: The Gritter title isn't big yet.
The Gritter title isn't purple yet.

hints: Make a new rule for the Gritter title's id.
Use #gritter with color and font-size.

steps.title: A reusable bold style
steps.instruction: At the bottom, write a rule for the class bold that sets the font weight to 900, the thickest.
steps.why: A class can be reused on as many parts of the page as you like.

checks.say: The bold sentence isn't extra thick yet.

hints: Make a rule for the bold label you put on the Gritter sentence.
Class rules start with a dot: .bold, using font-weight.

concept.title: Reusable classes
concept.explain: Unlike an id, one class can be put on many parts of a page to share the same look.

steps.title: Wrap-up
steps.instruction: Watch the summary of everything you built and learned.
steps.why: Looking back helps the ideas stick.
hints: Just watch.
Think about which part was newest to you.
Try changing a color in index.css to experiment.
